title: How a Pixar Intern and Conan O'Brien Created Toy Story 5's Funniest New Character
summary: Every Toy Story movie introduces memorable new toys, but Toy Story 5's Smarty Pants might be the most absurdly hilarious yet. Voiced by Conan O'Brien, this Fisher-Price-style potty-training device operates on critically low batteries, causing him to slur and stumble like a tipsy party guest. When cowgirl Jessie encounters him in a dilapidated playhouse, the result is instant comedy gold. Smarty Pants is a relic from Blaze, a girl who once owned Jessie's original kid, Emily. As Blaze grew, she abandoned Smarty Pants for newer tech toys like a GPS named Atlas and a digital camera called Snappy. Now, Smarty Pants fixates on the bathroom with a longing gaze, his entire worldview revolving around toilet time. O'Brien's chaotic energy brings the character to life, but the design itself has a charming origin story. Production designer Bob Pauley revealed that early concepts struggled—drawing literal pants or incorporating toilet imagery felt awkward. Then, in summer 2023, Pixar intern Naomi sketched a version that clicked. "She kind of drew the first Smarty Pants in the way he kind of looks now," Pauley said. The team evolved her idea into a nostalgic toy with an LCD screen and three buttons, making it feel like a hand-me-down from Blaze's toddler years. Pauley teased that Smarty Pants has a bigger role in the film's second half, and when animators combined the design with O'Brien's voice, it was "mind blowing." For O'Brien, it's a return to animation after his legendary Simpsons episodes, and Smarty Pants already seems poised to steal the movie.
why_it_matters: The creation of Smarty Pants shows how even a small sketch by an intern can shape a major movie, highlighting that creativity and collaboration can come from unexpected places—and that your idea might one day make millions laugh.

background_read: Toy Story, released in 1995, was the first fully computer-animated feature film and launched Pixar (the animation studio behind this and many other hits) into a new era of filmmaking. Each sequel introduces new toys that mirror childhood phases, often with clever designs based on real-life toys—Smarty Pants is a Fisher-Price-style potty-training device, tapping into the brand's long history of toddler products.

Conan O'Brien, before becoming a late-night talk-show host, was a writer for The Simpsons and penned iconic episodes like 'Marge vs. the Monorail,' so his return to animation marks a full-circle moment. Pixar's internship program has occasionally led to breakthroughs; in this case, a young artist's sketch solved a design puzzle that had stumped veterans, showing how fresh eyes can make a big difference.

The concept of a toy being replaced by newer, shinier gadgets echoes a common Toy Story theme: the fear of being outgrown. Smarty Pants was abandoned for a GPS named Atlas and a digital camera called Snappy, reflecting how real children often swap baby toys for tech devices as they age.

perspectives.description: Fans of Toy Story will enjoy the humor and nostalgia of a potty-training toy with a malfunctioning battery, and Conan O'Brien's chaotic voice adds star power to a beloved franchise. The origin story of an intern's sketch making it into the film also celebrates fresh talent.

Some may see the potty-training concept as too childish or low-brow for a series known for balancing wit and emotional depth, worrying that Smarty Pants could rely on easy toilet jokes instead of the sophisticated storytelling that made previous films classics.

Smarty Pants fits the Toy Story pattern of introducing toys that reflect different childhood stages—here, a toddler gadget abandoned for cooler tech—continuing the series' long-running commentary on growing up, obsolescence, and loyalty.

If Smarty Pants succeeds as a character, it could encourage studios to give more weight to ideas from young interns and lesser-known creatives, potentially leading to fresher, more diverse storytelling in future animated blockbusters.
